stem.text: Use the limit comparison test with \( \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{1}{n^{3}} \) to show that the series \( \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} a_n \), where \( a_n = \frac{\left(-1\right)^{n} \left(3 n + 9\right)}{2 n^{4} + 3} \), converges absolutely. State the conclusion, naming the series it concerns.

answer_key.label: \( \sum a_n \) converges absolutely, because \( \lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{|a_n|}{1/n^{3}} = \frac{3}{2} \) is positive and finite and \( \sum \frac{1}{n^{3}} \) converges.

worked_solution.text: Compare the series of absolute values \( \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{3 n + 9}{2 n^{4} + 3} \) with \( \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{1}{n^{3}} \), the p-series with \( p = 3 \), since the degrees of the denominator and numerator of the terms differ by 3. Both have positive terms.
The limit \( \frac{3}{2} \) is positive and finite, and \( \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{1}{n^{3}} \) converges because \( p = 3 > 1 \).
\( \sum a_n \) converges absolutely, because \( \lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{|a_n|}{1/n^{3}} = \frac{3}{2} \) is positive and finite and \( \sum \frac{1}{n^{3}} \) converges.

options.label: \( \sum a_n \) converges absolutely, because \( \lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{|a_n|}{1/n^{3}} = \frac{3}{2} \) is positive and finite and \( \sum \frac{1}{n^{3}} \) converges.
\( \sum a_n \) diverges, because \( \lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{|a_n|}{1/n^{3}} = \frac{3}{2} \) is greater than 1.
options.derivation: the limit of the quotient compared with 1, as in the ratio test, and found greater than 1

options.label: \( \sum a_n \) converges absolutely by the alternating series test, because \( |a_n| \) decreases to 0.
options.derivation: absolute values never taken, so only the alternating series test was used and its result called absolute convergence

options.label: \( \sum a_n \) converges conditionally, because \( \lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{|a_n|}{1/n^{3}} = \frac{3}{2} \) is positive and finite and \( \sum \frac{1}{n^{3}} \) converges.
options.derivation: the absolute and conditional labels exchanged after the series of absolute values was shown to converge
